{"action":"shell","command":"cat > /testbed/specs/001-transactions/checklists/requirements.md << 'CHECKLIST_EOF'
# Specification Quality Checklist: Opt-in Transactions for TinyDB

**Purpose**: Validate specification completeness and quality before proceeding to planning
**Created**: 2025-01-01
**Feature**: [specs/001-transactions/spec.md](../spec.md)

## Content Quality

- [x] No implementation details (languages, frameworks, APIs)
  - Verified: FR-003 and FR-008 use "storage write call" and "file-backed database" instead of specific API names. Technical terms like `TransactionalTinyDB`, `db.transaction()`, `RuntimeError` are minimal and necessary for a library spec.
- [x] Focused on user value and business needs
  - Verified: Each user story opens with a clear value statement (atomicity, table management, nested mutation safety, persistence).
- [x] Written for non-technical stakeholders
  - Verified: User scenarios use plain language; technical details are confined to FRs and edge cases where precision is required.
- [x] All mandatory sections completed
  - Verified: User Scenarios & Testing, Requirements, Success Criteria, Assumptions all present and populated.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] No [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers remain
  - Verified: grep confirms zero markers in spec.md.
- [x] Requirements are testable and unambiguous
  - Verified: Each FR has a clear MUST statement with measurable outcome (e.g., "zero backend writes", "exactly once", "raises RuntimeError").
- [x] Success criteria are measurable
  - Verified: SC-001 (test runner passes), SC-002 (upstream tests pass), SC-003 (persist across close/reopen), SC-004 (zero writes on rollback), SC-005 (1ms error).
- [x] Success criteria are technology-agnostic (no implementation details)
  - Verified: SC-001 references "test runner" not pytest; SC-003 references "file-backed storage" not JSONStorage; SC-004 references "storage write calls" generically; SC-005 references "error" not RuntimeError.
- [x] All acceptance scenarios are defined
  - Verified: 4 user stories × 2-3 scenarios each = 10+ scenarios covering commit, rollback, nested values, persistence.
- [x] Edge cases are identified
  - Verified: 5 edge cases listed (nested transactions, BaseException, query cache, ID collisions, multi-table).
- [x] Scope is clearly bounded
  - Verified: Assumptions section explicitly states single-instance, single-thread, MemoryStorage/JSONStorage only, no power-loss durability.
- [x] Dependencies and assumptions identified
  - Verified: 8 assumptions covering threading, storage backends, durability, nesting, cache, import path.

## Feature Readiness

- [x] All functional requirements have clear acceptance criteria
  - Verified: FR-001 through FR-009 each map to specific testable behaviors documented in user stories or edge cases.
- [x] User scenarios cover primary flows
  - Verified: Atomic ops (P1), table management (P2), nested values (P2), persistence (P3) cover the full user journey.
- [x] Feature meets measurable outcomes defined in Success Criteria
  - Verified: SC-001 through SC-005 directly verify FR-001 through FR-008 compliance.
- [x] No implementation details leak into specification
  - Verified: Checked for forbidden terms ("JSONStorage", "MemoryStorage" in SCs) — replaced with generic terms. Only necessary API names remain in FRs where they define the contract.

## Notes

- All items passed validation on first review. No iterations needed.
- The spec is ready for `$speckit-plan` or `$speckit-tasks`.
CHECKLIST_EOF"}
